subject: longitudinal measurement invariance with ordinal data

messages.author: a8cc7cfc6c0a8275
messages.subject: longitudinal measurement invariance with ordinal data
parts:
Dear all,

I am analyzing the longitudinal measurement invariance of two constructs seperately. My sample size is quite large (N = 2300). The calculation of configural and weak measurement invariance is no problem, there are just a few warnings regarding empty bivariate cells. I looked at them and do not much worry about it, because my constructs are both very skewed. My data is ordinal,I used the WLSMV estimator. When I test for the assumption of strong measurement invariance, I still get an ordinary looking output, but the fit-indices based on the WLSMV estimator are no longer calculated. The DWLS estimator produce fit statistics and I also get a  chi square fit statistic for the WLSMV estimator, but no RMSEA, CFI or WRMR. Do you knwo why it is not calculated?

Thanks a lot for your help, Angela

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: longitudinal measurement invariance with ordinal data
parts:
You also do not get any standard errors for this model. This suggests
that the information matrix for this model could not be inverted (and
this also explains why none of the robust fit statistics could be computed).

This is often a symptom that the model is not identified.

I noticed that you tried to impose equality constraints on the
intercepts, but they are (by default) fixed to zero when the variables
are ordinal. Try to impose equality constraints on the thresholds instead.

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: longitudinal measurement invariance with ordinal data
parts:
On 03/25/2015 09:38 AM, A.Bi. wrote:
> Thank you for your answer!
>
> I tried to impose equality constraints on the thresholds. But it does
> not work. Do I have an error in my syntax?

Yes.

This:

> dass3_t1|t1 ~ 1

is not a threshold. It should be:

dass3_t1 | t1

The '|' operator is the threshold operator. So the first three lines
(without equality constraints) should be

dass3_t1 | t1
dass3_t2 | t1
dass3_t3 | t1

For binary data, there can only be a single threshold ('t1'). To add the
equality constraints, you can either use the equal()* modifier:

dass3_t1 | t1
dass3_t2 | equal("dass3_t1|t1")*t1
dass3_t3 | equal("dass3_t1|t1")*t1

or use labels:

dass3_t1 | a*t1
dass3_t2 | a*t1
dass3_t3 | a*t1

Yves.
